result.title: Disentangling Robustness and Sycophancy in Multilingual LLMs
result.summary: When a multilingual LLM agrees with a user's false premise, is it being sycophantic, or does it simply not know better in that language? Current research does not distinguish these cases: they record only whether the model agreed, not why. We introduce the SC-matrix, that crosses a model's competence (whether it answers correctly under no pressure) with its sycophancy (whether it maintains that answer under pressure). Our results show that (1) identical aggregate sycophancy rates can mask different failure compositions, (2) high competence in a language does not always protect against sycophancy, and (3) reasoning-oriented mitigations outperform directive-based strategies. We find that multilingual sycophancy is not a single phenomenon but a composite of different failures that require distinct diagnosis.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SC-matrix，把多语言 LLM 在无压力下是否正确（能力）与受压时是否维持原答案（顺从）交叉分类，发现相同总体顺从率掩盖了不同失败构成，语言能力高并不必然抵御顺从，且推理导向的缓解优于指令式策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「知道」与「被说服」分开的二维诊断思路可能可供核查：或可移用于区分 VLM 答案是来自视觉证据还是文本先验与用户前提顺从。
